content: Without virtue, man is the most unholy and the most savage of animals, and the most full of lust and gluttony.
author: Aristotle
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. True wisdom is rarely complicated or flashy, but it demands the honesty to look at our own habits and assumptions without defensive excuses.

Across his life and work, Aristotle saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. When you stop looking for external validation and anchor your self-worth in quiet integrity, the noisy chaos of the world loses its power over you. A good life is built day by day through small, conscious choices.
reflectionPrompt: What long-held assumption about your life or abilities is challenged by this insight?

originalQuote: The man who is not virtuous is the most unholy and savage of animals, and the most full of lust and gluttony.
